liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (1 review, 1 other source): Acoustic Truckin' is very rare, with Pigpen on piano; Per deadlists.com, Pigpen plays piano on Truckin' [3][15]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (2 reviews): The Sugar Magnolia on this download is weak; the 9-18 version on other copies is far hotter; Reviewer became a Dead fan by the end of Sugar Magnolia and doubts a better version exists, perhaps 11-6-70 [10][14]
- **Dancin' In The Street** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Dancin' from the soundboard source a monster and the show's best part; Jerry plays hard on a roughly 19:30 Dancin' [7][9]
- **Black Peter** (1 other source): Per deadlists.com, David Nelson plays mandolin on Black Peter [3]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Casey Jones is called a perfect opener to the Dead's electric set [14]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One has sweaty, energetic jamming [7]
- **Operator** (1 review): Operator is rarely played; this soundboard makes it audible, though vocals are a bit low, unlike other audience copies [15]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Good Lovin' runs about 21 minutes and is picked as the best performance, with Pigpen going all out [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Workin' Man Blues**: rare: 14 archived performances [18]
- **Superman**: rare: 10 archived performances [18]
- **Rainbow**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [18]
- **Dirty Business**: rare: 12 archived performances [18]
- **Glendale Train**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 13 archived performances [18]
- **Sawmill**: rare: 6 archived performances [18]
- **It's A Man's World**: rare: 11 archived performances [18]
- **Till The Morning Comes**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 6 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd70-09-18.sbd-aud.cotsman.17893.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 32 songs; 199 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience-source dropouts hit Candyman and the first Cryptical Envelopment, leaving both nearly unlistenable; Honky Tonk Women through Till the Morning Comes is poor audience quality; the first five tracks and Me and My Uncle onward are soundboard [7][12]
- **gd70-09-18.set2.aud-sbd.sirmick.sbeok.30882.flacf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 116 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: The early audience-source portion sounds poor; quality improves greatly at Me & My Uncle, when the soundboard takes over; The first part of the show is a poor-sounding stealth-style recording, earning only two stars for sound; Reviewer wishes a soundboard existed for the first part of the show [9][13][14]
- **gd70-09-18.bootleg.evans.100.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 7 songs; 71 min; rated 4.86/5 by 7 [4]. Said about its sound: Sound quality of this copy is mediocre, though the playing and song choices are strong; The better Sugar Magnolia versions on the other 9/18 downloads sound worse than this one; A brief reel glitch occurs in Dancin' at 5:06 [4][8][10]
- **gd1970-09-18.sbd.reynolds.97525.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 80 min; rated 3.12/5 by 8 [3]

## Around the show

- Dustin Hoffman was on stage during intermission, filming Harry Kellerman [11]
- The Dead came on at midnight and played until almost 6:00 am [11]
- Torrential rain fell, rumors circulated that Jimi had died, and Tim Leary and later Mayor Lindsay sat in adjacent seats [11]
- The band played until sunup, then played again for free in Central Park [17]
- A New Riders set fell between the Dead's acoustic set and their electric set [1]
- The acoustic set was cut short by technical difficulties [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-09-18.sbd-aud.cotsman.17893.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jack Toner; transferred by Andy Lemieux, Jack Warner, JCotsman; source: Soundboard and Audience composite [1]. Also: The soundboard supplies the acoustic set and Me & My Uncle onward; the rest of this matrix is audience [1]
- **gd70-09-18.set2.aud-sbd.sirmick.sbeok.30882.flacf**: transferred by SIRMick; source: Soundboard (remaster) [2]. Also: Remaster of an earlier matrix: soundboard covers Me & My Uncle to the end, the rest is Jack Toner's audience tape; The uploader left the soundboard section alone apart from tweaking the patch in Dancin' and re-encoding to FLAC [2]
- **gd70-09-18.bootleg.evans.100.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Morgan Evans; source: Unknown [4]. Also: The Dark Star on this bootleg-derived copy comes from a different show, not this one; Source traced to the Haight Street Records bootleg 'Fall of Another Year', with filler from other shows added [4][8]
- **gd1970-09-18.sbd.reynolds.97525.flac16**: transferred by Chuck Reynolds; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [3]
